statement: In Kentucky, a person at least 18 years old may have their name changed by the District Court of the county where they live. If you live on a United States Army post, military reservation, or fort, the District Court of an adjacent county may do it instead.
detail: Once the court orders the name change, a copy is certified to the county clerk, who keeps an alphabetical index of every name change for that county. The Kentucky Court of Justice's self-help portal does not publish its own instructions for this process; it points people to a third-party guided-interview website instead.

cost.note: A filing fee applies; the district court clerk sets and collects it. Kentucky's statute does not publish the amount on this page, so ask the clerk for the current fee.

source.title: Kentucky Revised Statutes 401.010 — Adult May Have Name Changed by District Court

topic: Kentucky driver's license or ID name change
statement: To change the name on a Kentucky driver's license or ID card, first update your name with the Social Security Administration. Then bring your updated Social Security card and legal documentation, such as a court order, to a Driver Licensing Regional Office in person.
detail: Kentucky's Transportation Cabinet says name changes must be completed in person and cannot be done online or by mail. You receive a temporary credential right away, and your permanent card typically arrives by mail within 10 to 15 business days.

cost.note: This is Kentucky's fee for an in-person name change on a driver's license or ID card.

timeline.typical: 10-15 business days for the permanent card by mail

source.title: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet — Update or Replace a Driver's License or Permit

topic: Kentucky driver's license or ID gender marker
statement: Kentucky's Transportation Cabinet does not publish a separate form or process for changing only the gender marker on a driver's license or ID card. Its own FAQ page only mentions that a name-change document is needed if your current legal name, date of birth, or gender differs from what your identity documents show.
detail: We could not find an official Kentucky Transportation Cabinet page describing a standalone way to change a driver's license or ID card's gender marker on its own, separate from your underlying identity documents. That absence is not evidence Kentucky has no such process — only that we have not found one published online. Contact a Driver Licensing Regional Office directly to ask what it requires before relying on this record.

statement: Kentucky amends the name on the birth certificate of a person born in the Commonwealth once the Office of Vital Statistics receives a certified copy of a court order changing that person's name.
detail: File the notarized VS-2J Affidavit for Amendment along with the certified court order with the Office of Vital Statistics. A registrant who is 18 or older signs their own affidavit; a parent or legal guardian signs for someone younger.

cost.note: This is the fee for a certified copy of the corrected birth certificate. If a certified copy issued within the past year is returned to the Office of Vital Statistics, a corrected copy is issued without an additional charge.

source.title: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services — VS-2J Affidavit for Amendment to Certificate

statement: Kentucky law only allows the gender on a birth certificate to be amended after a licensed physician swears that the person's gender has been changed by surgical procedure, and only together with a certified copy of a court order changing that person's name.
detail: Both requirements come from the same state law and must be submitted together on the VS-2J Affidavit for Amendment; Kentucky's Office of Vital Statistics describes no other path to amend this field. This surgical-procedure requirement is considerably more restrictive than what many other jurisdictions in this corpus require, and it has been in Kentucky law since 1990.

cost.note: This is the fee for a certified copy of the corrected birth certificate.

source.title: Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services — VS-2J Affidavit for Amendment to Certificate
